ARABIC LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #8
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ARABIC LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. How is the Arabic word مَسَاءُ الْخَيْرِ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. marhaban
   B. masaa'u l-khayr
   C. as-salaamu ʿalaykum
   D. sabaahu l-khayr

2. Which Arabic word means "peace be upon you"? (1 mark)
   A. السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ
   B. شُكْرًا
   C. كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟
   D. صَبَاحُ الْخَيْرِ

3. What does the Arabic sentence أَنَا تِلْمِيذَةٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I am a pupil (boy).
   B. I am from Kenya.
   C. I am a pupil (girl).
   D. My name is Ahmad.

4. What does the Arabic word عَمٌّ (ʿamm) mean? (1 mark)
   A. father's brother
   B. mother's brother
   C. grandmother
   D. father's sister

5. What does the word al- do at the start of an Arabic word? (1 mark)
   A. It means 'the'
   B. It means 'my'
   C. It means 'and'
   D. It means 'not'

6. How is the Arabic word عِنْدَ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. ʿalaa
   B. ʿinda
   C. taHta
   D. bijaanibi

7. Which day is al-jumuʿa? (1 mark)
   A. Friday
   B. Sunday
   C. Wednesday
   D. Saturday

8. What does the Arabic sentence أَلْعَبُ يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. Today is Thursday.
   B. I go to school on Monday.
   C. There are seven days in a week.
   D. I play on Saturday.

9. What does the Arabic sentence أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ يَوْمَ الِاثْنَيْنِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I go to school on Monday.
   B. I play on Saturday.
   C. Today is Thursday.
   D. There are seven days in a week.

10. Which is a good way of reducing food waste? (1 mark)
   A. Throw away leftovers
   B. Take only what you can eat
   C. Leave food outside uncovered
   D. Cook more than needed

11. How is the Arabic word سَمَكٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. bayd
   B. milh
   C. samak
   D. maa'

12. How is the Arabic word حَلِيبٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. bataatis
   B. haliib
   C. bayd
   D. faakiha

13. Which Arabic sentence means "I smell with my nose." (1 mark)
   A. أَتَكَلَّمُ بِفَمِي
   B. أَسْمَعُ بِأُذُنِي
   C. أَشُمُّ بِأَنْفِي
   D. أَنَا أَرَى بِعَيْنِي

14. What does the Arabic sentence أَتَكَلَّمُ بِفَمِي mean? (1 mark)
   A. I smell with my nose.
   B. I see with my eye.
   C. I hear with my ear.
   D. I speak with my mouth.

15. How is the Arabic word مُشْمِسٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. jamiil
   B. shajara
   C. mushmis
   D. jabal

16. What does the Arabic word شَمْسٌ (shams) mean? (1 mark)
   A. sunny
   B. weather
   C. sun
   D. flower

17. How do you read the syllable سِ? (1 mark)
   A. si
   B. laa
   C. tu
   D. mu

18. How do you read the syllable بِي? (1 mark)
   A. bi
   B. laa
   C. bii
   D. qaa

19. How do you read the syllable لَا? (1 mark)
   A. bii
   B. si
   C. du
   D. laa

20. Which Arabic word means "house"? (1 mark)
   A. كُوبٌ
   B. حَمَّامٌ
   C. نَافِذَةٌ
   D. بَيْتٌ

21. How is the Arabic word أَمْسِ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. al-yawm
   B. al-ithnayn
   C. al-jumuʿa
   D. amsi

22. What does lii ʿaynaani mean? (1 mark)
   A. You have two ears.
   B. I see with my eye.
   C. My eye is big.
   D. I have two eyes.

23. Which Arabic sentence means "I have two eyes." (1 mark)
   A. لِي يَدَانِ
   B. جِسْمِي قَوِيٌّ
   C. لِي عَيْنَانِ
   D. هَذَا جِسْمِي

24. How is the Arabic word مَطَرٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. matar
   B. shams
   C. riih
   D. nahr

25. What sits on the baseline in Arabic writing? (1 mark)
   A. Only the vowels
   B. Nothing
   C. Most of the letters
   D. Only the dots

26. What is the name of the Arabic letter د? (1 mark)
   A. khaa
   B. daal
   C. Haa
   D. Saad

27. Which Arabic word means "family"? (1 mark)
   A. أُخْتٌ
   B. أُسْرَةٌ
   C. ابْنٌ
   D. جَدَّةٌ

28. Which Arabic word means "carrots"? (1 mark)
   A. جَزَرٌ
   B. مَوْزٌ
   C. ذُرَةٌ
   D. فَاكِهَةٌ

29. Which Arabic word means "finger"? (1 mark)
   A. إِصْبَعٌ
   B. كَتِفٌ
   C. قَلْبٌ
   D. وَجْهٌ

30. Which Arabic word means "clean"? (1 mark)
   A. غَائِمٌ
   B. نَظِيفٌ
   C. زَهْرَةٌ
   D. شَجَرَةٌ

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Translate into English: ʿalaa t-taawilati kuub (2 marks)

32. Name three things that make Arabic writing different from English writing. (3 marks) (3 marks)

33. Translate into English: hal tuhibbu l-mawz? (2 marks)

34. Explain why your family members are important to you. Give two examples of roles. (3 marks) (3 marks)

35. Explain why we should show respect when we greet people of a different gender or culture. (3 marks) (3 marks)

36. Translate into English: atakallamu bi-famii (2 marks)

37. Copy and translate the sentence أُحِبُّ الْخُبْزَ. (2 marks) (2 marks)

38. Explain how a family celebration you know helps people to live together in peace. (3 marks) (3 marks)

39. Translate into English: ayna l-kitaab? (2 marks)

40. Translate into English: uhibbu l-mawza (2 marks)

41. Give three questions you could ask when you give peer feedback on a friend's fluency. (3 marks) (3 marks)

42. Write three Arabic questions about a picture of a party and give their meanings. (3 marks) (3 marks)

43. Translate into English: al-maa'u nadhiif (2 marks)

44. Translate into English: al-jawwu haarr (2 marks)

45. Translate into English: marhaban yaa Ahmad (2 marks)

46. Write four weather words in Arabic sounds with meanings. (4 marks) (4 marks)

47. Translate into English: usaaʿidu ummii yawma s-sabt (2 marks)

48. Translate into English: anaa araa biʿaynii (2 marks)

49. Translate into English: anaa fii S-Saffi r-raabiʿ (2 marks)

50. Say what the words abii yaʿmalu and ummii tatbukhu mean, and name one thing each parent does. (4 marks) (4 marks)
pages.answers:
ARABIC LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #8 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — masaa'u l-khayr
   مَسَاءُ الْخَيْرِ is read masaa'u l-khayr and means good evening.

2. A — السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ
   السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ (as-salaamu ʿalaykum) means peace be upon you.

3. C — I am a pupil (girl).
   أَنَا تِلْمِيذَةٌ (anaa tilmiidha) means: I am a pupil (girl).

4. A — father's brother
   عَمٌّ (ʿamm) means father's brother.

5. A — It means 'the'
   al- is the word for 'the', as in al-kitaab, the book.

6. B — ʿinda
   عِنْدَ is read ʿinda and means at (near, by).

7. A — Friday
   al-jumuʿa is Friday.

8. D — I play on Saturday.
   أَلْعَبُ يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ (alʿabu yawma s-sabt) means: I play on Saturday.

9. A — I go to school on Monday.
   أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ يَوْمَ الِاثْنَيْنِ (adhhabu ilaa l-madrasa yawma l-ithnayn) means: I go to school on Monday.

10. B — Take only what you can eat
   Taking only what you can eat and saving leftovers reduces waste.

11. C — samak
   سَمَكٌ is read samak and means fish.

12. B — haliib
   حَلِيبٌ is read haliib and means milk.

13. C — أَشُمُّ بِأَنْفِي
   أَشُمُّ بِأَنْفِي (ashummu bi-anfii) means: I smell with my nose.

14. D — I speak with my mouth.
   أَتَكَلَّمُ بِفَمِي (atakallamu bi-famii) means: I speak with my mouth.

15. C — mushmis
   مُشْمِسٌ is read mushmis and means sunny.

16. C — sun
   شَمْسٌ (shams) means sun.

17. A — si
   سِ is read si.

18. C — bii
   بِي is read bii.

19. D — laa
   لَا is read laa.

20. D — بَيْتٌ
   بَيْتٌ (bayt) means house.

21. D — amsi
   أَمْسِ is read amsi and means yesterday.

22. D — I have two eyes.
   lii means I have and ʿaynaani means two eyes.

23. C — لِي عَيْنَانِ
   لِي عَيْنَانِ (lii ʿaynaani) means: I have two eyes.

24. A — matar
   مَطَرٌ is read matar and means rain.

25. C — Most of the letters
   Most letters rest on the baseline. Alif stands tall above it.

26. B — daal
   The letter د is called daal.

27. B — أُسْرَةٌ
   أُسْرَةٌ (usra) means family.

28. A — جَزَرٌ
   جَزَرٌ (jazar) means carrots.

29. A — إِصْبَعٌ
   إِصْبَعٌ (isbaʿ) means finger.

30. B — نَظِيفٌ
   نَظِيفٌ (nadhiif) means clean.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: On the table there is a cup.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is written from right to left; it has no capital letters; most letters join and change shape; short vowels are shown with marks.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid difference.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: Do you like bananas?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: They love and care for us. For example parents work, cook and pay for school; grandparents share stories and advice; children help at home.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for love and care, 2 marks for two correct roles.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Greeting customs can differ. Using polite words and a smile shows respect. Respect helps boys and girls, men and women to be treated equally and to live peacefully.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for customs differ, 1 mark for polite words, 1 mark for equality or peace.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: I speak with my mouth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: uhibbu l-khubza. I like bread.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a correct copy or sounds and 1 mark for the translation.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: People meet, share food and joy, sing and talk together, and learn to respect one another.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meeting, 1 mark for sharing, 1 mark for respect.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: Where is the book?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: I like bananas.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Were the words clear? Was the speed steady? Did the voice fall for statements and rise for questions?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each suitable question.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example ayna l-kaʿka? (Where is the cake?) man haadhaa? (Who is this?) maadhaa fawqa t-taawila? (What is above the table?)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct question with meaning.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: The water is clean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: The weather is hot.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Hello, Ahmad.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example shams (sun), matar (rain), riih (wind), sahaab (clouds).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with meaning.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: I help my mother on Saturday.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: I see with my eye.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: I am in Grade 4.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: abii yaʿmalu: My father works. ummii tatbukhu: My mother cooks.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each translation and 1 mark for each role named.
